content_preview.summary: EDB announced the acquisition of Altinity on November 5, 2026; terms were not disclosed, integrated ClickHouse offerings are planned for Q4 2026, and two analysts quoted by TechTarget say integration work remains.

editor_notes.content_quality: News article of about 815 words (script count), structured as Overview, What the companies announced, What EDB says comes next, What analysts say, What We Don't Know. Every attribution is explicit (release, Altinity's own post, Blocks & Files, TechTarget). Vendor characterisations (largest commercial Postgres contributor, #2 independent ClickHouse contributor) are labelled as EDB's own and the absence of contribution data is stated. The October 26 Herald link is described accurately. Tone neutral; the only loaded-language hit is 'clearly', which sits inside a quotation of Blocks & Files.
editor_notes.source_verification: Snapshots read from disk after gunzip and HTML-to-text extraction, sha256 of each decompressed file re-computed and equal to the manifest value; all four fetched with HTTP 200, no archive fallback, suspicious_patterns null for all four. source-0 (PR Newswire, sha256 103d22d0...e49e811, EDB release dated Nov. 5, 2026, 08:49 ET): confirms 'today announced the acquisition of Altinity, a leading independent provider of enterprise software, managed services, and support for ClickHouse software'; 'EDB plans to introduce integrated enterprise ClickHouse capabilities in Q4 2026' (the plan is EDB's; the object is 'capabilities'); four deployment modes (BYOC; developer cloud; self-hosted / on-premises on customer-managed Kubernetes or OpenShift; physical far edge for air-gapped, fully disconnected execution); 'The integration road map includes a shared Apache Iceberg catalog and consistent access controls across Postgres and ClickHouse software'; 'Capability and deployment availability will be detailed as offerings are introduced'; founded 2017; customers The Trade Desk, Tubi, Kong, AppsFlyer, ZoomInfo, PostHog; Stable Builds, Antalya Builds, Kubernetes Operator 'with more than 108 million Docker Hub pulls', Altinity.Cloud; 'Altinity's engineers join EDB's Postgres contributors and maintainers'; non-affiliation notice ('not ClickHouse, Inc.', 'Altinity is an independent company and is not affiliated with ClickHouse, Inc.'); 'EDB is already the largest commercial contributor to Postgres, and Altinity is the #2 independent contributor to ClickHouse software' in a quoted paragraph whose speaker the release does not name (raw HTML line follows Kevin Dallas's quote); the release says nothing about price. source-1 (altinity.com, sha256 f926ca72...a8d7a61f, post by Robert Hodges dated 5th November 2026): confirms 'Altinity is now the EDB Real-Time Analytics group, reporting directly to the EnterpriseDB CEO, Kevin Dallas', contracts, SLAs, products and services the same, 'The entire management team remains in place'; states EDB is '#1 commercial contributor'; no price. source-2 (Blocks & Files, Chris Mellor, published Fri 6 Nov 2026, sha256 31a71971...a660b208): confirms 'Financial terms for the acquisition were not revealed. Altinity raised $4 million in a 2020 seed round.'; PGAA ('Postgres Analytics Accelerator') and WarehousePG ('an open-source massively parallel processing (MPP) analytical database forked from Greenplum'); 'EDB clearly needs more OLAP capability.' (verbatim); attributes the 'largest commercial contributor' / '#2 independent contributor' paragraph to Dallas, which supports the article's attribution; carries no ClickHouse, Inc. statement. source-3 (TechTarget, Eric Avidon, Senior Reporter, Data, Published Nov. 5, 2026, sha256 04eff9ce...fe8c92): confirms 'Financial terms of the acquisition were not disclosed'; 'Near-term product development plans include developing a shared Apache Iceberg catalog and consistent access controls'; 'first added support for ClickHouse earlier this year'; Pratt (IDC analyst) 'EnterpriseDB can now cover both the operational and analytical sides of the estate from one vendor' (verbatim), prior customers 'had to use databases from other providers', competitors 'AWS, Google Cloud, Databricks, Snowflake and independent PostgreSQL providers', acceleration but 'it doesn't complete the evolution', ClickHouse capabilities 'expected before the start of 2027', 'Altinity adds the analytics engine, [but] integrating it is the real test' (bracket is TechTarget's); Aslett (analyst at ISG) 'There will be considerable engineering work to be completed before the company can deliver on that promise', 'with two separate environments', the ClickHouse Managed Postgres context and 'Altinity is a direct competitor to ClickHouse Inc.'s portfolio of software, services and support'. Titles: TechTarget calls Pratt 'an analyst at IDC' (article says 'of IDC', no title claimed); the release and Blocks & Files give 'research director at IDC', not used by the article for him. All 10 quoted strings in the article were matched verbatim to the snapshot text. Quantifiers and absence claims tested against all four snapshots with the jq/grep pass: 'Both TechTarget and Blocks & Files report that financial terms were not disclosed' holds (not disclosed / not revealed); 'The sources report no deal value' holds (no price in any source); 'none of the cited sources gives a date for either [Iceberg catalog, access controls]' holds; 'None of the four cited sources includes a statement from ClickHouse, Inc.' holds (TechTarget quotes none; the only ClickHouse Inc. text is the non-affiliation notice written by EDB/Altinity). Dates: Nov 5, 2026 is a Thursday, matching TechTarget's 'on Thursday'. No relative dates in the article. Herald link /article/2026-10/26-postgres-vendors-take-... resolves to a published article; its HFS Research (Ashish Chaturvedi) summary of EDB 'keeps PostgreSQL as the operational source of truth and exposes data through Iceberg to analytical engines' matches the article's description; that article has a corrections record (clarification on the plural 'analysts' in its title), which does not touch the passage the new article relies on. Allowlist: altinity.com and techtarget.com were not listed; both confirmed and added with justification comments in config/source_allowlist.txt (altinity.com: github.com/Altinity org, API 'blog' field https://www.altinity.com, description 'Leading Service and Software Provider for ClickHouse'; techtarget.com: named staff byline Eric Avidon with staff profile techtarget.com/editors/eavidon/ returning 200, footer 'Editorial Team' link /editors/, NewsArticle with no sponsored label). prnewswire.com and blocksandfiles.com were already listed. Suspicious patterns: none flagged in any manifest entry. Scanner warning 'Contains loaded language' (pattern definitely|absolutely|obviously|clearly) is a false positive: the only match is 'clearly' inside the quotation of Blocks & Files, 'EDB clearly needs more OLAP capability', which the article attributes and quotes verbatim; the Herald does not use the word in its own voice. Independent-source recount: 2 independent outlets (Blocks & Files, TechTarget), 2 first-party (EDB release, Altinity post). Blocks & Files largely reproduces the release (quotes, customer list, roadmap text) but adds its own reporting: EDB's earlier PGAA and WarehousePG approach, the OLAP editorial view, the 2020 seed round and the terms statement. TechTarget adds original reporting: interviews with IDC and ISG analysts and EDB's chief product officer, the ClickHouse Managed Postgres context and the 2027 timing. The article uses each only for what it adds. Anthropic disclosure: not required - the article is about EDB and Altinity; Anthropic is not named.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No wrong statement found in the headline, summary or lead; every figure, name, date and quote traces to a snapshot. Observations: (1) the article attributes the 'largest commercial contributor' quote to Dallas as 'the release quotes Dallas'; the release's paragraph is unattributed in its own text, but Blocks & Files attributes the same continuous text to Dallas, so the attribution stands. (2) 'The Altinity release' in the paragraph linking the October 26 analysis refers to the EDB release about Altinity; the rest of the article calls it 'the release', so context makes it clear. (3) The last 'What We Don't Know' bullet speaks of 'no statement from the company beyond the release's non-affiliation notice'; that notice is written by EDB and Altinity, not by ClickHouse, Inc., as the Overview section already states. Not corrected. (4) The headline compresses two descriptions: 'ClickHouse support provider' (the release says Altinity provides 'enterprise software, managed services, and support'; Altinity's GitHub organisation describes it as 'Leading Service and Software Provider for ClickHouse') and 'integrated offerings' (the release says 'integrated enterprise ClickHouse capabilities', although it uses 'offerings' in the next sentence). Both are incomplete rather than wrong, and the lead and body give the full wording, so one clarification record is filed. Title is 136 characters, under the 150 limit.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; vendor claims are attributed to the vendor and the 'largest/#2 contributor' ranking is flagged as unsupported by contribution data in the cited sources. No sensational wording, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. No existing article on EDB/Altinity; the only related piece is the October 26 Postgres-vendors analysis, linked from the article and added as a related article in the meta file.
concerns: Headline wording compresses Altinity's description ('support provider') and the planned item ('offerings' for 'capabilities'); recorded as a clarification in src/content/corrections/2026-11/.
Blocks & Files is a lightly reworked relay of the press release with a small amount of added context, so the effective independent corroboration for analysis rests on TechTarget.
recommendations: Use the release's own noun for the object of a plan in headlines ('capabilities') or the vendor's full description of a company, rather than a shortened label.
When a release quote has no named speaker, say that and cite the outlet that attributes it.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced News piece on a defined announcement; all quotes and figures verified verbatim against raw snapshot text. Approved with one clarification on headline wording. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid acquisition story for database and data-platform readers with terms and delivery details still undisclosed
